annotations.title: Check a name against trademark registers

description: Read-only trademark check for ONE proposed name, answered by Open Trademarks (opentrademarks.org) from the US, EU and Israeli trademark registers. Nothing is filed, reserved, watched or paid for. Optional `goods` (free text, mapped to Nice classes), `classes` (Nice classes 1 to 45) and `registers` (a subset of `us`, `eu`, `il`; all three by default) narrow the check. Read `verdict` first. `exact_live_mark` and `similar_live_marks` name the marks behind them in `conflicts`, each with its register, number and how it matched. `no_live_match` means no live mark matched in the registers that were read: a positive signal, not clearance. `not_checked` means no register in this check has been read yet, so it is NOT a verdict: do not call the name clear or taken on it. `registers` gives each register's read date, and a register with no `loaded_at` was not checked at all. Never tell a user a name is clear unless it was checked during this conversation and every register in the answer was read today or yesterday. Quote `notice` as written: a register search is not legal advice. Use it when the user is choosing or vetting a name for a brand, product or business. It checks trademarks only: for whether a domain is available or what it costs, use `search_domains`; for moving a domain the user already owns at another registrar to Just Domain, use `check_domain_transfer`.

classes.description: Optional: Nice classes to check, each 1 to 45 (e.g. [9, 42]).

goods.description: Optional: what the name will be used for, in plain words (e.g. 'accounting software'). Open Trademarks maps it to Nice classes.

name.description: The proposed name, as the user would use it (e.g. 'Acme' or 'koh-i-noor'). One name per call.

registers.description: Which registers to read: a subset of `us`, `eu` and `il`. All three when left out.
